Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1439.xml). Chan Master Weilin Daopei’s Fragrant Meal Record. Konggu Daocheng owns the retained deployment: instructing on faith: trust it through, and the three-times buddhas walk arm in arm, the ten-direction tathagatas sit together in one stupa — delusion and enlightenment lacking nothing, exceeding nothing, commoner and sage at par — while love's insistence on the innate bright wonder is what makes the six roads of turning.

Senses.Explanation: Lacking nothing, exceeding nothing. The tag is Sengcan's: the Xinxin Ming line 圓同太虛，無欠無餘 — round and whole like the great void, nothing short of it, nothing over it — and the masters keep it welded to that void-roundness. Zhongfeng Mingben, weighing the ancestor's instruments, rules that the boundless ocean-lands, the ten-times past-and-present, the dust-grain dharma-gates and the hundred-thousand samadhis all sit inside the one shout and the one stick — wholly gathered, wholly taken in, lacking nothing, exceeding nothing — and then turns on the freak-show tricksters he says have filled the ages since, mistaking worm-cry and dust-tossing for that grasp. Huanyou Zhengchuan, instructing without punctuation, follows the mind everyone originally has — no shape to find anywhere in the ten directions, unmoving, one body with the void, never born, never extinguished, neither square nor round, neither large nor small, neither soiled nor clean, neither increasing nor decreasing, nowhere present yet nowhere absent — lacking nothing, exceeding nothing, everywhere-yet-not-a-place: the one listening to this old monk right now, lone and bright. Weilin Daopei, raising the medicine case — Sudhana finds nothing on the whole earth that is not medicine, plucks one stalk of grass and hands it to Wenshu, who holds it up: this medicine can also kill, can also give life — rules: the whole earth is sickness, the whole earth is medicine; with such medicine treating such sickness, lacking nothing, exceeding nothing, just right; though it only cures the one who has the sickness — if a sickness-less one comes, how do you treat him? Yinyuan Longqi, at the winter solstice, releases the season: this side does not allow long standing, that side will not brook dwelling; letting out one stretch of spring, everything unfolds — surging east, sinking west, lacking nothing, exceeding nothing, at the mercy of wind and sun, free before lightning and thunder; ride the horse if there is a horse, ride the donkey if there is none — and when there is neither horse nor donkey, what do you ride? Yunwai Xingze, at his inauguration, points at the seat before mounting it: this jeweled flower-king seat rests forever on the crown of every one of you, not wide, not narrow, lacking nothing, exceeding nothing; you cannot push it away, you cannot climb up it — why not go straight down like this? If you cannot yet, this mountain monk will lift it off for you. Gusu Zun, after running the four exchanges of deprivation and non-deprivation to their last shout, rules: each person's own single move beneath himself is truly round and whole like the great void, lacking nothing, exceeding nothing. Huizhou Hao, closing the summer, traces it behind the beginning: every being, from before the Bhishma-sounding kalpa, realized enlightenment together with the buddha-ancestors, lacking nothing, exceeding nothing — only one speck of unresolved delusion and they fell back, unknowing; hence the hundred thousand devices, all to wake each to the face they already are. And Konggu Daocheng, instructing on faith: trust it through, and the three-times buddhas walk arm in arm, the ten-direction tathagatas sit in one stupa; delusion and enlightenment lack nothing, exceed nothing, commoner and sage stand at par — know this innate bright wonder, never increased, never soiled, and the six roads of turning are only love's insistence.
